comment: He's a super nice guy and makes his lectures very engaging. You can tell he knows a lot and really cares about what he's teaching. There's no homework except for short journal responses once a week and weekly readings, but he talks about them in class so you don't really need to read them. There's just three short reflective essays and a midterm.
Amazing professor, very passionate, as long as you pay attention in class and scan readings you are good. Midterm is the only really hard thing in the class, and essays are not hard at all

Evan Welchance is my literal goat, I love that guy. Lectures could sometimes be boring, but if you enjoy philosophy you'll love them (I absolutely despise Philosophy so the lectures were rough). Very accessible and was a huge help whenever I had questions. The whole class was pretty straight forward and not too difficult. 100% would recommend!!!

Dr. Welchance is very passionate about philosophy & his passion is clear in his lectures.  He constantly ensures students understand by providing analogies, examples in everyday life, & pausing to clarify important points.  Extremely approachable and available during office hours.  Homework is very minimal and always reasonable, esp for philosophy.

Great guy and really passionate about philosophy. Lectures were him talking and essays were graded hard, especially considering many students had never interacted w philosophy before. Readihgs arent too bad but you never know what part hes gonna focus on in class. I wouldn't recommend for gen ed

Professor Welchance is very passionate about Philosophy and explains topics well. While he is accessible outside class, he is a very tough grader, which makes it difficult if you do not have prior knowledge of philosophy. Homework is minimal and he takes the full week to explain one reading, which is necessary and helpful.

He's easy enough. Just show up, answer a few questions, and do the weekly journal entry. The midterm was simple, but also hard in that you didn't really know what to study for despite him giving you the topics. It was curved though. The most tough thing was that he didn't provide a really clear rubric for papers, which made writing them a bit hard.
Made the class more work than it needed to be, somewhat unclear grading rubrics
